advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Enforce that a 'created' CreateSignal carries a non-None known_key (raise or degrade to commit_unknown) rather than emitting applied/known_key=None.
evidence: Docstring at create_coordinator.py:57 '#: A "created" signal MUST carry a non-None key; the ambiguous statuses re-observe.'
_created (create_coordinator.py:141) returns Disposition.applied with known_key=signal.known_key and no None-check
No test exercises CreateSignal(status='created', known_key=None) — searched test file, (no matches)
advisory.finding: A 'created' CreateSignal with known_key=None yields an applied CreateOutcome carrying known_key=None, silently violating the module's own documented invariant that a 'created' signal MUST carry a non-None key (and AC5 'whenever created a key is known'). _created copies signal.known_key through with no validation.
scenarios: An adapter bug or partial response returns status='created' without a key; the op is reported applied with no recoverable identity, defeating later convergence.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _created (or _resolve_create's created branch), raise/assert or route to commit_unknown when signal.known_key is None.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _resolve_create reject unrecognized CreateSignal.status values explicitly (mirror failure_policy.status_to_disposition's ValueError) instead of defaulting unknowns to permanent.
evidence: _resolve_create (create_coordinator.py:222): if status=='created' ... elif in _AMBIGUOUS ... else return _permanent(plan, signal)

Docstring at create_coordinator.py:48 enumerates statuses as created/timeout/connection_lost/permanent, but the code never checks status=='permanent' explicitly — everything else falls into _permanent
Sibling failure_policy.status_to_disposition raises ValueError on an unknown status (failure_policy.py:124-127), showing the established contract is to FAIL LOUDLY on unknown statuses
_resolve_ambiguous (create_coordinator.py:216-219): observation=observe(plan); if observation.status=='proven': recover; else commit_unknown
ObservationSignal docstring (create_coordinator.py:69) declares only 'proven'/'inconclusive' as valid statuses, but neither is asserted
commit_unknown diagnostic records signal.status (the CREATE status), not observation.status, so a bad observation status leaves no trace
advisory.finding: _resolve_create maps ANY CreateSignal.status not in {'created','timeout','connection_lost'} to _permanent via a silent else-branch. An unknown or misspelled status (adapter contract drift) becomes a permanent_failure indistinguishably from a genuine permanent error — a lookup MISS that is invisible instead of a loud failure.
merged_from: _resolve_ambiguous treats every observation status other than 'proven' as commit_unknown, so a malformed/unexpected ObservationSignal.status (not the documented 'inconclusive') is silently folded into the deferred path with no distinguishing signal — the observation oracle cannot distinguish 'checked and inconclusive' from 'received a bad status'.
scenarios: create_execute returns a new/typo'd status (e.g. 'throttled'); it is silently reported as permanent_failure with no diagnostic distinguishing it from a real permanent error.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an explicit `if signal.status == 'permanent': return _permanent(...)` branch and raise ValueError on any other status.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a permanent-create test with a non-default (e.g. endpoint) signal.scope asserting outcome.failure_scope reflects it.
evidence: Source _permanent returns `_outcome(plan, Disposition.permanent_failure, signal.scope, ...)` — failure_scope is driven by signal.scope (added line).

Test: `create_mod.CreateSignal(status="permanent", scope=S.ticket, diagnostic="bad request")` and asserts `outcome.failure_scope == S.ticket`, but S.ticket is the CreateSignal default `scope: object = FailureScope.ticket`.
Named violating input: a `CreateSignal(status="permanent", scope=FailureScope.endpoint)` would expose whether signal.scope is actually propagated; no test drives a non-default scope.
advisory.finding: The permanent-create test passes scope=S.ticket (the CreateSignal default), so it cannot distinguish _permanent's propagation of signal.scope into failure_scope from a hardcoded FailureScope.ticket; a regression that ignored signal.scope would still pass.
scenarios: A refactor that hardcodes FailureScope.ticket in _permanent instead of reading signal.scope.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a case passing CreateSignal(status="permanent", scope=FailureScope.endpoint) and assert outcome.failure_scope == FailureScope.endpoint.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert CreateOutcome.diagnostics content for the persist-failure (incl. no-args fallback), permanent (present and None), and commit_unknown paths.
evidence: search_files for 'diagnostics' in the test file: (no matches).

Source _pending_save_failed extracts `message = str(diag[0]) if diag else exc.__class__.__name__` and packs `diagnostics=({"stage": "persist_pending", "message": message},)` — added lines with a two-way branch.

Source _permanent builds diagnostics only `if signal.diagnostic is not None` else empty tuple — added branch untested (test_permanent passes diagnostic='bad request' but asserts nothing about diagnostics).
Named violating input: a persist raise of `RuntimeError()` with no args exercises the `exc.__class__.__name__` fallback, which no test drives.
advisory.finding: No test asserts on CreateOutcome.diagnostics, leaving the added diagnostic-building branches (persist-failure message extraction, permanent create diagnostic present-vs-None, commit_unknown category) uncovered.
scenarios: A create with signal.diagnostic=None; a persist exception with empty args.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_ac1 assert `outcome.diagnostics == ({"stage": "persist_pending", "message": "store write failed"},)` and add an args-less RuntimeError case; in the permanent test assert the create diagnostic tuple and add a diagnostic=None case.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Relax the AC6 signature test to assert the delete/undo tokens are absent and the required seams are present, rather than exact set equality.
evidence: `assert kw_only == {"persist_pending", "create_execute", "observe", "budget_factory"}` — exact-set equality on the introspected signature.
The following assertion already enforces the actual AC6 contract: `assert not any(tok in name for name in kw_only for tok in ("delete", "undo", "rollback", "unbind"))`.
advisory.finding: test_ac6_no_delete_injectable_exists asserts the keyword-only parameter set with exact equality, which breaks on a behavior-preserving addition of any unrelated seam while adding nothing over the adjacent delete/undo/rollback/unbind token check.
scenarios: A future no-op addition of a metrics/telemetry keyword-only callable that does not add a delete seam.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the exact-equality assertion with `assert {"persist_pending", "create_execute", "observe"} <= kw_only` and keep the forbidden-token check.
